title: The Dyatlov Pass Mystery
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the 1959 Dyatlov Pass incident, in which nine experienced students from the Ural Polytechnic Institute died during a winter ski trip in the northern Urals. They describe the abandoned tent cut from the inside, the bodies found barefoot and in underwear near a cedar tree and later in a gully with severe internal trauma, the radioactive clothing, the last photo on the camera, and the Soviet investigation that closed the case and classified its files. They then discuss theories including missile tests, UFOs, avalanche, Mansi tribe attack, high winds, infrasound, and the questioned identity of Simon Zolotarev. The episode closes with listener mail from Corey in Jersey City about a supposed earlier tsunami episode that the hosts mistakenly believed they had already done.

segments.title: Intro and pronunciation of Dyatlov Pass
segments.summary: Hosts introduce the episode as an Unsolved Mysteries edition, settle on pronunciation of Dyatlov, and mention a personal Russia travel anecdote.

segments.title: The hiking group and the trip
segments.summary: Nine experienced students from the Ural Polytechnic Institute set out in early February 1959 for Mount Otorten. One member, Yuri Yudin, turned back sick. The group kept a fun group newspaper diary, and the hosts describe the members' relationships.

segments.title: Camp site choice and missing contact
segments.summary: The group camped on an exposed slope on the night of February 2 rather than in the forest a mile below. Something happened before dinner. The search began late because the planned return timeline was vague.

segments.title: Discovery of the tent and first bodies
segments.summary: Searchers found the tent cut open from inside and the group's gear and boots left behind. Two bodies were found barefoot and in underwear near a cedar tree, with signs of a fire and broken branches.

segments.title: Remaining bodies and internal injuries
segments.summary: Three more bodies were found between the tent and the tree, then four more in May in a gully. The latter had severe internal injuries, crushed skulls and chest fractures, and one woman was missing her tongue. Officials said no outside trauma was visible.

segments.title: Radioactive clothing, the camera, and the Soviet cover-up
segments.summary: Some clothing was radioactive. The camera's final frame showed a bright light. The investigation was closed with a vague cause of death, the files were classified, the area was closed for three years, and parts of the files were missing when declassified.

segments.title: Sightings of lights and UFO reports
segments.summary: Witnesses reported bright flying objects and orange fireballs in the area that month. Some theorized these were missile tests or UFOs that irradiated the group.

segments.title: Theories: avalanche, Mansi attack, wind, infrasound, and Zolotarev
segments.summary: The hosts assess an avalanche theory, the Mansi tribe attack theory (rejected for lack of footprints), the high wind theory, and the infrasound theory. They also discuss Simon Zolotarev, a late addition whose identity was questioned after DNA testing.
